crime: Every evening, a girl waded barefoot through the lake shallows for one flat stone for the little stone hut she was building on the shore. "A house of my own, one stone a day," she said. Most evenings {WITCH_NAME} came down and sat in the grass, telling her where she would go next.
One evening the girl laid a doorstep stone before the hut, with {WITCH_NAME}'s name scratched into it. "Now you live here. There is no further on."

When {WITCH_NAME} was small, her father loaded the cart while she sat on the doorstep of each rented house. "The real house is further on," he would say. She had said it of every place she stood ever since.

She rose from the grass and took one step, and landed ankle-deep in the water behind the girl, who was bending for tomorrow's stone. She drove the girl's head down onto the stones and held her face under until she was still. Then she stepped back out of the water in one stride.

At dusk a prisoner found the girl face down at the water's edge. Her shoes sat on the sand, and only her own bare footprints crossed it to the water. In the trial court, the prisoners held that she had slipped on the stones, struck her head and drowned alone.

But that dawn, before the trial, a prisoner had looked into the clear shallows on the lake side of where she lay. Shoe prints were pressed into the bottom in one spot, with no trail leading to them or away. The prisoners saw what it meant: someone in shoes had stood beside her without ever crossing the sand, and only {WITCH_NAME}'s single step could land that way.
fields.epitaph: Every horizon was a single step away, every one but a doorstep with her name on it.
fields.epithet: The Girl Whose Real Home Is Always Further On
execution: The execution stand lays her on her back across a doorstep stone scratched with her name, strapped flat beside a heap of flat lake stones. One by one, it lays the stones on her, starting at her feet and working upward. The walls of a little house rise around her, and its roof stones settle across her chest. Pinned beneath the first stones, her feet keep trying to take one step. At last the stone house stands finished on the stand, her name on its doorstep, and nothing stirs inside.

magic.name: Seven-League Step
magic.text: One ordinary step carries her as far along her way as she wishes.
